extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal agencies, USPTO stakeholders, patent and trademark practitioners, and the public
extracted.subtask_description: Official USPTO Performance and Accountability guidance covering (a) substantive patentability and trademark registrability standards and examiner duties, and (b) agency performance metrics and reporting/validation rules for patent and trademark operations. Intended to inform agency management, practitioners, and oversight bodies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patentability requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners review patent applications to determine whether the claimed invention is eligible for patent protection, useful, adequately disclosed, and clearly defined; they compare the claimed invention to a large body of technical information to determine whether it is novel and non-obvious.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This enumerates the classic substantive statutory and examination standards: subject-matter eligibility, utility, adequate written description and enablement (disclosure), clarity of claims, novelty (new), and inventive step/non-obviousness. Examiners perform searches of prior art and compare claims to existing technical information; they also respond to appeals and prepare PCT preliminary examination reports.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of patents and statutory terms
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three types of patents: Utility (may be granted for any new and useful process, machine, article of manufacture, composition of matter, or useful improvement), Design (new, original, ornamental design for an article of manufacture), and Plant (new, distinct, asexually reproduced plant variety).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Utility patent term generally 20 years from filing (subject to PTAs/PTEs and maintenance fees); Design patents 14 years. Patent grants confer the right to exclude others; patentees must enforce rights themselves (USPTO does not enforce).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Term Adjustment (PTA) and pendency measurement
rubrics_metrics.description: PTA is tracked to measure the USPTO's adherence to statutorily defined timeframes; tracking PTA provides a refined description of pendency and indicates consistency in meeting required timeframes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO reports PTA compliance metrics such as 'PTA Compliance - Mailed Actions' and 'PTA Compliance - Remaining Inventory.' Example: FY2021 met these time frames in 83% of all office actions mailed. USPTO notes that focusing on PTA may affect average first-action pendency (older applications addressed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examination performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency-level performance metrics include measures such as PTA compliance (mailed actions and remaining inventory), average first-action pendency, average total pendency, percent of office actions meeting timeframes, and Exceptional Office Action rate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAR provides target and actual values for FY21 (e.g., PTA Compliance targets/actuals, first-action pendency in months, total pendency). Performance results are summarized with color/status (Green/Red) and are used in strategic reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performance target attainment rule
rubrics_metrics.description: A performance result of a given measure is either met (100% or greater of target) or not met (99.9% or below of target).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the USPTO's binary rule for reporting whether targets were achieved; reported measures in the PAR use this threshold to determine Green (met) vs. Red (not met) statuses.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent examiner qualifications and duties
rubrics_metrics.description: Patent examiners are highly skilled professionals with backgrounds in science, engineering, and graphic design/art and are responsible for reviewing applications to determine eligibility, usefulness, disclosure adequacy, clarity, novelty, and non-obviousness; they search electronic and non-patent literature, respond to appeals, and prepare PCT preliminary examination reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners receive designated training programs (Patent Examiner Training); duties include prior-art searching, preparing office actions, handling appeals to PTAB, and contributing to international examination cooperation. Examiner staffing levels, attrition rates, and training are tracked in the PAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark registrability criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademarks (and service marks) must meet the requirements of the Trademark Act of 1946; core determinations include whether marks are used in commerce and whether pending or registered marks are confusingly similar to the subject application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Trademark examining attorneys search databases for confusingly similar marks, prepare communications and office actions, approve applications for publication, examine statements of use under Intent-to-Use (section 1(b)), and evaluate maintenance documents and renewals. Registrability determinations include refusals based on likelihood of confusion and failure to meet use-in-commerce requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark performance metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark performance measures reported include Average First Action Pendency (months), Average Total Pendency (months), First Action Compliance Rate, Final Compliance Rate, and Exceptional Office Action percentage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAR lists FY21 targets and actuals (e.g., trademark first action pendency target 4.5 months, actual 6.3 in FY20 vs. 4.5 target FY21 and FY21 actual 6.3 shown for earlier year example). Compliance rates are reported as percentages (e.g., First Action Compliance 95.5% target, 96.3% actual). These metrics are used to evaluate timeliness and quality in the Trademarks organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark Modernization Act (TMA) implementation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The TMA of 2020 provides tools to clear the federal Trademark Register of unused marks and enables more efficient processing; implementation requires new rules and procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: USPTO conducted public roundtables and comment periods to gather feedback for rulemaking and shaped final decisions based on stakeholder input. Implementation requires procedural rulemaking, operational changes, and outreach/training for examining attorneys.

rubrics_metrics.name: PTAB and review procedures post-Arthrex
rubrics_metrics.description: Following the Supreme Court decision in United States v. Arthrex, Inc., the USPTO posted interim procedures for parties to request Director review of PTAB final decisions in inter partes and post-grant reviews; USPTO solicited input and refined procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interim procedures establish a mechanism for Director review of PTAB decisions; USPTO invited public comment and may further refine procedures based on experience with Director reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data verification, validation, and reporting requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance data included in the PAR must be verified and validated; the Performance Information section describes key and supporting performance metrics and how results were verified/validated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAR includes a Performance Data Verification and Validation subsection and uses audited financial statements and independent auditors' reports to support claims of data completeness, reliability, accuracy, and consistency. Performance audits and evaluations are documented in the report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency strategic goals tied to quality and timeliness
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO's mission-focused strategic goals explicitly include: Goal I — Optimize Patent Quality and Timeliness; Goal II — Optimize Trademark Quality and Timeliness; Goal III — Provide Domestic and Global Leadership on IP Policy, Enforcement, and Protection Worldwide; Mission Support Goal — Deliver Organizational Excellence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These strategic goals drive performance metrics, staffing, training, IT modernization (e.g., DOCX transition and Patent Center), international cooperation, and policy initiatives described throughout the PAR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner search and evidence resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiners are expected to search both patent and non-patent literature and use available electronic databases and collections to compare claimed inventions to existing technical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAR tracks use and growth of non-patent literature collections, full-text electronic journals/books, and databases available for searching; the agency emphasizes improving collections and machine/Manual translation resources for examiner support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights conferred by a patent and enforcement responsibility
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent grant confers the right to exclude others from making, using, offering for sale, selling, or importing the invention in the United States; it is not a positive right to practice the invention. Once issued, the patentee must enforce the patent without the aid of the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAR clarifies scope of rights and notes that enforcement is a private matter for patentees (e.g., district court litigation or other enforcement channels). It also notes availability of Patent Term Extensions (PTEs) and adjustments (PTAs) in certain circumstances.

rubrics_metrics.name: USPTO funding and fee-setting framework
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO operations are funded completely by user fees; fee-setting authority and performance-based attributes have been shaped by various statutes including the Omnibus Budget Reconciliation Act of 1990 and the AIA (which provided temporary fee-setting authority).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The PAR discusses how fee policy, legislative mandates (e.g., SUCCESS Act), and fee-setting authority affect USPTO's sustainable funding model and resource planning. Biennial review of user fees and federal rulemaking related to fee adjustments are part of administrative requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trademark use-in-commerce and limits of trademark protection
rubrics_metrics.description: Trademark rights arise from use in commerce and registration prevents others from using a confusingly similar mark, but does not prevent others from making the same goods or selling the same goods under a clearly different mark.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrations require use in interstate or foreign commerce to be registered with USPTO; the PAR underscores the public notice function of the registration database and the maintenance/renewal processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stakeholder engagement and rulemaking transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: When implementing major legal changes (e.g., TMA), the USPTO conducts public roundtables and solicits stakeholder comments to inform rulemaking and operational decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PAR cites examples (three public roundtables for TMA implementation) and emphasizes stakeholder input as part of transparent rulemaking and policy development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality assurance and continuous improvement expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: USPTO emphasizes continuous evaluation and optimization of operations and patent/trademark quality management, including training, IT modernization, and performance measurement to improve customer satisfaction and examination quality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples include Patent Center and DOCX adoption to streamline filing and improve data quality, investments in cloud IT, training programs, and tracking customer satisfaction. The PAR cites earning an unmodified audit opinion and no material weaknesses as indicators of financial/operational control.
